video_goal: Demonstrate the correct visual sequence for threading a climbing rope into a Petzl Grigri and securing it to a harness with a locking carabiner.
required_subjects_and_props: Petzl Grigri belay device, dynamic climbing rope, pear-shaped locking carabiner, climbing harness

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands hold a bright orange Petzl Grigri belay device in the left hand and a thick dynamic climbing rope in the right hand.
The left thumb pushes the black plastic release handle slightly to pivot and slide open the metal moving side plate of the Grigri.
The right fingers pinch the climbing rope, folding it over to form a tight, U-shaped bight.
The bight of rope is pushed into the open Grigri, wrapping the curve of the rope around the internal grooved metal cam.
The camera focuses on the engraved icons inside the Grigri, showing the top strand of rope aligning with the 'climber' icon and the bottom strand aligning with the 'hand' icon.
The metal moving side plate is pivoted back into its original position, snapping shut over the seated rope.
A right hand brings a pear-shaped locking carabiner into the frame, positioning it next to the closed Grigri.
The carabiner gate is pushed open with the thumb, and the nose of the carabiner is hooked through the two aligned metal attachment holes of the Grigri.
The carabiner, now holding the Grigri, is pushed downward to clip through the thick nylon belay loop of a worn climbing harness.
Fingers twist the textured metal sleeve on the locking carabiner upward until it stops, visibly covering the nose of the gate.
The left hand sharply pulls the top 'climber' side of the rope upward, while the right hand firmly grips the bottom 'brake' side of the rope downward.
The internal cam of the Grigri visibly pivots upward inside the device, pinching the rope tightly against the metal channel to arrest the upward pull.
